title: @file_get_contents + json_decode swallow failures silently — the caller gets null, not an error
sourceContent:
<?php
// fetch_price.php - fetch a remote price, swallowing errors
function fetchPrice($url) {
    // TRAP: @ suppresses the warning if the URL is unreachable; on
    // failure file_get_contents returns FALSE, then json_decode(false)
    // returns null, so the failure is silently swallowed.
    $body = @file_get_contents($url);
    $data = json_decode($body, true);
    return $data['price'] ?? 0.0;
}
notes: The @ operator suppresses the warning and file_get_contents returns false on failure; json_decode(false) yields null, so a network/parse failure is silently swallowed and the caller gets 0.0 with no signal. The migration must classify this as a swallowed error and use try/catch + a typed exception. The remote fetch is a side effect; the ?? is a null-safety default.
